transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess the main thing is my sleep… it’s been going on for such a long time that I almost got used to it, but I’m just worn out. I’ll fall into bed completely exhausted, like my body is done for the day, but then I don’t really sleep well. Every little sound in the house wakes me up — the floor creaking, a door, whatever — and once I’m awake it’s like I’m not fully resting anymore.

And then I’m up before the alarm most mornings, just lying there feeling like I never actually slept. It’s not like I wake up refreshed. I wake up already tired, and it’s been wearing on me. That’s really what brought me in.
Do you find yourself worrying or feeling anxious when you're lying in bed awake?

I don’t know that I’d call it anxiety exactly. I mean, I’m not lying there having a full panic feeling or anything like that, at least not that I’ve noticed. It’s more like… once I’m awake, I become very aware that I’m awake, if that makes sense. Then I start noticing the time, and the quiet, and how tired I already feel, and I get frustrated because I know morning is coming.

But as far as worrying about specific things, I’m not sure. Sometimes my mind is just kind of on, but I wouldn’t say there’s one clear thing I’m afraid of or worrying about every night. It’s more that I’m awake and annoyed and tired, and then that makes it harder to settle back down.
Do you feel tired or lacking in energy during the day?

Yes. Very much, honestly. By the time I’m done seeing my home-health clients, I feel like I’ve already used up everything I have. And then I still have to come back and help at home, and it’s like my body just gets heavy… not sleepy exactly all the time, but drained, like I’m moving through mud.

Even small things feel bigger than they should. Like charting my notes after visits — something I know how to do, something that shouldn’t be such a big deal — I’ll sit there staring at it because it feels like too much effort to push through. Or folding laundry, just regular household stuff, I’ll look at the basket and feel like I can’t make myself start. I do it because I have to, but it takes so much out of me. It’s been really frustrating.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood lately?

Yes… I think so. It’s hard to explain without sounding dramatic, but most days it feels like the color has gone out of things. Like I’m there, I’m doing what I’m supposed to do, I’m talking to people, I’m going through the motions, but everything feels kind of dimmed.

Even at Sunday dinner with my family, which should feel nice — and sometimes I can tell, logically, that it is nice — I’ll just be sitting there feeling this heaviness come over me. Not even because anything bad happened. I’ll look around and everyone’s eating and talking, and I’m trying to be normal, and I’ll suddenly feel like I might cry. I have to really work to hold it together.

And art, too… I used to really enjoy looking at art, like it would make me feel something, or I could get lost in it a little. Now I’ll look at something I know I would’ve liked before, and it’s like there’s this glass wall between me and it. I can see that it’s beautiful, but I don’t feel it the same way. That’s been happening most days, I’d say.
Are there things that you used to enjoy doing, but no longer find pleasure in?

Yes… yes, definitely. I guess the biggest one is art. I used to really enjoy it — not even necessarily making anything, just looking at it, going to a gallery if I had the chance, or even just seeing something beautiful and feeling kind of pulled into it. It used to give me this little lift, like it opened something up in me.

Now I can look at the same kind of thing and I know, in my head, that it’s beautiful, but I don’t really feel it the way I used to. It’s like there’s glass between me and it. And that’s hard to explain, because I’m still there, I’m still seeing it, but the pleasure part just doesn’t come through.

Even with family things, like Sunday dinner, I should enjoy that. I know I should. Everyone’s talking and eating, and nothing is wrong exactly, but I’ll be sitting there and it’s like the color has gone out of everything. I feel this heaviness, and sometimes I have to work really hard not to tear up, even though I couldn’t tell you one clear reason why. So yes, things I used to enjoy just feel… muted now.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in?

I mean… I’m trying to think of one, and I guess there are moments where I can tell something should be pleasant, if that makes sense. Like if I’m at Sunday dinner with my family, I know that’s supposed to feel good — people are together, there’s food, everyone’s talking — and there may be a second where I think, “This is nice.” But it doesn’t really land the way it used to.

Most days it just feels like the color has gone out of things. Even with art, which used to be one of the things I could count on to enjoy, I’ll look at something and know it’s beautiful, but I don’t feel that little spark from it anymore. It’s more like I’m observing it from behind glass.

So… I don’t know if I’d say there’s much I truly find pleasure in right now. There are things I still do, and things I know I should enjoy, but a lot of the time there’s this heaviness there, and sometimes I have to work really hard not to tear up for no clear reason.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It’s been… a little over two years now, I think. It really started around when my mother-in-law moved in with us. I don’t know if I noticed it all at once, exactly — it wasn’t like one day I woke up and everything felt different — but when I look back, that’s the point I keep coming back to.

At first I think I told myself I was just adjusting, you know, because having another person in the house changes the whole rhythm of things. But then months went by, and then more months, and this feeling just sort of stayed. So yes… a little over two years. Since she moved in with us.
Are there any activities that you still look forward to or feel excited about?

Not really… I wish I could say yes, but I don’t think I feel excited about much these days. I still go through the motions with things, like Sunday dinner with my family, and part of me knows that should be something I look forward to. I mean, it’s family, it’s familiar, it’s warm in theory. But when I’m actually there, sitting at the table, listening to everyone talk, it’s like everything is sort of dulled down.

And with art, too — that used to be something I could get excited about, or at least feel drawn toward. I could see something beautiful and feel it, almost physically, like it reached me somehow. Now I can look at art and recognize that it’s beautiful, but it doesn’t really stir anything up in me.

Most days it just feels like the color has gone out of things. And sometimes I’m doing something completely normal, something that should be pleasant, and I’ll feel this heaviness come over me and have to work hard not to tear up. There isn’t even always a clear reason for it, which makes it feel worse in a way, because I can’t point to one thing and say, “That’s why.” It’s just… there.
Have you noticed any changes in your relationships with friends or family members since you started feeling this way?

I’m not sure I’ve noticed a clear change, exactly. I mean… I know I probably seem different to people, but it’s hard for me to tell what’s really changed in the relationships themselves versus what’s just going on inside me.

With family, I still see them, still talk, still show up. I don’t think there’s been some big falling-out or anything like that. But I guess I sometimes feel more distant, even when I’m physically there. Like I can be sitting with people I care about and still feel kind of separate from the whole thing. I don’t always know if they notice that, though.

With friends… I don’t know. I wouldn’t say I’ve had some dramatic change, like cutting everyone off. It’s more that I’m maybe not as engaged as I used to be. But it’s hard to measure, because life gets busy anyway, and everyone has their own things going on. So I don’t want to overstate it.

I guess the honest answer is: I haven’t really noticed a specific change I can point to, but I do feel less present with people sometimes.
Have you had any periods in the past two years where you felt significantly better for a while?

Not really, no. I mean, there have been days here and there where I got through things a little easier, or maybe I was distracted enough that I didn’t think about it as much. But I wouldn’t say there was a real stretch where I felt like myself again, or where it lifted in any meaningful way.

It’s more like… ever since my mother-in-law moved in with us, a little over two years ago, this has just been sort of there in the background all the time. Some days it’s quieter, I guess, and some days it feels heavier, but I can’t point to a few weeks or a month where I thought, “Oh, I’m better now.” It’s just been ongoing since then.
Have you had two years or more of persistent feelings of sadness or loss of interest?

Yes… I think so. I mean, when I really look at it honestly, it’s been going on since my mother-in-law moved in with us, and that was a little over two years ago now.

It’s strange because it doesn’t feel like I marked it on a calendar at the time, like, “this is when everything changed,” but looking back, that’s the point where it started to settle in and just… stay. There may have been better days mixed in, but the sadness and the lack of interest, that dulled feeling, has been there pretty consistently since then.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to enjoy most of the time?

Yes… most of the time, I think that’s fair to say. It’s not that I can’t physically do things, or that I never go through the motions, but the feeling I used to get from them just isn’t really there.

Like Sunday dinner with my family — I’m there, I’m sitting at the table, people are talking, it should feel warm or familiar or something. And sometimes I’m looking around and it’s almost like the color has gone out of it. I know these are people I love, and I know it’s supposed to matter to me, but inside it feels kind of flat, or far away.

And art too… I used to really enjoy looking at art, noticing colors and details and feeling something from it. Now I can still look at it, but it doesn’t land the same way. It’s like I’m waiting for that little spark to come back and it just doesn’t.

A lot of days I feel like I’m working hard just to seem normal, honestly. Sometimes I’ll be doing something ordinary and I’ll feel tears coming up for no clear reason, and I’m trying to hold it together because I don’t even know how to explain it. So yes, I’d say I’ve lost interest, or at least the enjoyment has mostly drained out of things.
Are your feelings of sadness and lack of interest usually present for most of the day, or do they come and go?

It’s usually there most of the day, honestly. It’s not like I wake up fine and then something happens and I suddenly get sad, or like it comes in neat waves. It’s more like this dull layer over everything.

Even if I’m doing something that should feel nice, like sitting at Sunday dinner with my family, I’ll look around and feel like the color has gone out of the room somehow. Or I’ll look at art, which used to really pull me in, and I’m just… there, looking at it, but not feeling much from it.

There are moments when I’m distracted, sure, or I’m busy enough that I’m not actively thinking about how sad I feel. But underneath it, it’s still kind of sitting there. And sometimes out of nowhere I’ll feel like I might tear up, for no clear reason, and I have to work pretty hard to keep it together. So yes, I’d say it’s present most of the day, most days.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms have been present for most of the day
doctor.question: Are your feelings of sadness and lack of interest usually present for most of the day, or do they come and go?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Most days I feel like the color has gone out of things, even when I'm sitting at Sunday dinner with my family or looking at art I used to enjoy, and I have to work hard not to tear up for no clear reason.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about how persistently sadness and loss of interest are present during the day, which most directly relates to the persistent depressed mood symptom.

patient.answer:
It’s usually there most of the day, honestly. It’s not like I wake up fine and then something happens and I suddenly get sad, or like it comes in neat waves. It’s more like this dull layer over everything.

Even if I’m doing something that should feel nice, like sitting at Sunday dinner with my family, I’ll look around and feel like the color has gone out of the room somehow. Or I’ll look at art, which used to really pull me in, and I’m just… there, looking at it, but not feeling much from it.

There are moments when I’m distracted, sure, or I’m busy enough that I’m not actively thinking about how sad I feel. But underneath it, it’s still kind of sitting there. And sometimes out of nowhere I’ll feel like I might tear up, for no clear reason, and I have to work pretty hard to keep it together. So yes, I’d say it’s present most of the day, most days.
